comparison: Strong agreement on core experimental findings. Both affirm that mismatches increase nucleosome stability through DNA cyclization (C20, C63) and fluorescence-force spectroscopy (C21, C22, C32, C33) data. OpenEval emphasizes complementary experimental approaches and controls (C26-C28), while peer reviewers explicitly state findings are 'compelling' with 'important data.' Both also address cycle-dependent changes (C29-C31) that OpenEval separates into R2. Peer review groups these together as part of core findings.

OpenEval separately evaluates cycle-dependent unwrapping force changes (C29-C31) as SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic interpretation is speculative. Peer reviewers include these claims in their overall affirmation of core findings without separately questioning the repositioning mechanism, suggesting acceptance of the documented phenomenon.

Perfect agreement (100% claim overlap). Both affirm the ED2 control experiment (C35) demonstrates localized mismatch effects and asymmetric behavior (C36). Peer Reviewer 2 explicitly confirms 'CC mismatch only affects the local unwrapping dynamics,' matching OpenEval's assessment that this strengthens the local flexibility model.

Both support quantitative flexibility comparisons and cyclization data (C38-C40, C63). OpenEval emphasizes the ~7-fold convergence and position-dependent effects, while peer reviewers confirm the cyclization assay validates CC as most flexible mismatch. Peer R3 includes control data (C43-C45) that OpenEval separates into R5.

Partial overlap on sequence-dependent flexibility claims (C67-C69). OpenEval R4 focuses on quantitative comparisons between mismatch and sequence effects, while Peer R7 addresses broader consistency with prior work (C66) and mechanistic interpretations (C70-C71). Both affirm the flexibility-stability relationship.

Both address tether position controls (C43-C45). OpenEval emphasizes these as rigorous controls addressing potential artifacts from prior work, while peer reviewers include these as part of broader cyclization validation without separate commentary. Both find the controls adequate.

Perfect agreement (100% claim overlap). Both affirm the systematic survey of eight mismatch types (C46) and pattern of C-containing mismatches being most flexible (C47). Peer Reviewer 3 explicitly notes correlation with independent buckling assays, while OpenEval notes some quantitative discrepancies with prior EFRET values but accepts general trends.

Both address mechanistic distinctions between mismatch and sequence-induced flexibility (C70-C71). OpenEval finds this sophisticated interpretation SUPPORTED by comparative data, while peer reviewers accept the consistency with prior work (C66-C69) without challenge. Both affirm the flexibility-stability relationship across perturbations.

Perfect agreement (100% claim overlap). Both affirm species comparison data showing yeast nucleosomes have lower stability and increased symmetry (C24-C25, C48-C53). Peer reviewers explicitly confirm 'asymmetric unwrapping was more pronounced for yeast histones,' matching OpenEval's assessment. OpenEval notes bimodal distribution suggesting heterogeneity.

Perfect agreement (100% claim overlap). Both support interpretations connecting histone sequence differences (C54-C55) to mechanical stability (C58). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes causal connection remains inferential, while peer reviewers accept the structural/sequence explanations without challenge, with editor noting 'appropriate text additions.'

Significant disagreement on biological interpretation. OpenEval rates mechanistic model connecting stability to mutation accumulation (C23, C72-C73, C76) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's speculative without direct evidence. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'biological significance and implications remain unclear,' directly questioning this claim. Both recognize limitations (C77-C79).

Both address discussion caveats and limitations (C77-C79). OpenEval includes these in UNCERTAIN evaluation of biological model, while peer reviewers accept these as appropriate caveats added during revision. Agreement that limitations are acknowledged, but grouped differently with other claims.

Both address consistency with prior work (C66) on flexibility-stability relationship. OpenEval emphasizes this strengthens generalizability but notes kink mechanism (C64) is speculative. Peer reviewers affirm consistency with previous findings from same group without separately questioning mechanism.

Both address prediction for future work (C80). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting it's logical but untested extrapolation. Peer reviewers accept this as appropriate discussion point without challenge, suggesting it was added or refined during revision and deemed acceptable speculation.

OpenEval evaluates methodological context about 601 sequence limitations (C59-C60) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these background/methodological claims were not separately addressed by reviewers.

OpenEval rates speculation about alternative functional implications (C62) as UNCERTAIN, noting it's untested hypothesis. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not separately address this speculative point.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C19) as SUPPORTED established knowledge. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - reviewers did not separately assess background/context claims, focusing instead on novel findings.
